I should keep my reply concise: the prototype is clickable and saved at tmp/living-desk.html, but the scores shown are scripted rather than real Jev output. I want to be upfront that the idea of rolling up per-paragraph scores into a whole-draft grade is unvalidated, since the current rubric only produces one whole-draft score per criterion.

I'll also flag that the stance ledger's "we" counting is just a regex that doesn't yet distinguish different kinds of collective voice the way Jev does — something the prototype already surfaces but I shouldn't over-explain. I'll recommend Phase 1 be the living skeleton and keep the whole response tight.

content.text:
You're right, I'd narrowed it to sentences. I've reworked `docs/writing-instruments.md` around six levels (word, sentence, paragraph, section, piece, collection). Above the sentence level, the new pieces are:

- **Consistency ledgers.** Code finds every occurrence of something across the piece, and Jev judges only the ambiguous ones. They cover I/we stance, narrating tense, point of view within a scene, spelling of names, terminology drift, and a copyeditor's style sheet. Each one can be fixed one at a time or all at once, or marked **Deliberate**. Deliberate adds a Charter rule, so the ledger stops flagging the mix but still catches new drift.
- **Characters and entities.** Every character is tracked across sections, so you can see who drops out and where. The doc also covers relationships and how their tension changes chapter by chapter, and continuity checks for details like a character's age or a coat that changes colour.
  - One test I think is new: hide who is speaking and ask Jev to guess the speaker of each line. If Mara's lines keep getting attributed to Tom, the two characters sound alike.
- **Structure.** Outline headings get small markers for share of the piece, open problems and score. Each promise the piece makes is tracked as kept, open or dropped. Pacing curves run alongside the outline.

## The living score

The prototype above is clickable, but its numbers are scripted, not real model output. It's saved at `tmp/living-desk.html`.

The rubric can't do this today. It asks Jev for one score per criterion over the whole draft, and only reviews drafts of 500+ words, at most once every 30 seconds after a save. So the grade can't point to where it comes from, and it can't move while you edit.

The proposal updates at three speeds:

- **Instantly, in code:** counts, the style sheet, and the static features. `scoreStaticFeatures` already exists; it's just only called at review time.
- **When a paragraph settles:** Jev rescores that paragraph against the criteria a paragraph can show, like evidence, integrity, pacing and voice.
- **Periodically:** a full-piece read rescores criteria like thesis and structure, and confirms the estimate.

Each card's impact is roughly the criterion's weight × the gap to the next score level × how much of the piece is affected. Cards are ordered by impact, so the one that matters most comes first.

One untested assumption: I don't yet know whether rolling paragraph scores up into a grade matches what a whole-piece read gives. That's why the estimate is marked ≈ and is replaced by the confirmed full read when it arrives. We'd need to check it on real drafts before the estimate can be trusted.

## Next step

I've re-ordered the phases. Phase 1 is now the "living skeleton":

- the common card shape;
- the document spine beside the page;
- the lens system that highlights one problem across the manuscript;
- live static scoring;
- the code-only ledgers: style sheet, name variants, I/we counts, and who appears where.

All of it works offline. The I/we ledger classified by Jev comes right after, in Phase 2. Should I start building Phase 1 in the editor?

content.thinking:
I'm thinking about how to split the work between Codex and Sonnet: the backend implementation covers the core engine—pure TypeScript modules for ledgers, live static scoring, card schema/impact, document indexing, the ProseMirror extension wiring for lens decorations, and Jev classification for stance detection.

For frontend (Sonnet, low effort), I'm scoping out the document spine component, a card list UI, a lens toggle, a live score header with criterion bars, the ghost preview/fix application interface, and matching CSS in the global stylesheet.

Since both agents will work on the same checkout with a dirty working tree, I need to define shared types and interfaces upfront as a contract so Codex and Sonnet can work in parallel without conflicting edits.

I'll write the contract file first myself — a types module covering the card schema, ledger occurrences, lens definitions, snapshot store, and controller API — then have the backend agent implement the engine and editor extension that publishes snapshots and exposes controller methods like applyFix, applyAll, markDeliberate, and setLens, while the frontend agent consumes those snapshots through an event or store to render the UI. To get the contract right, I should quickly check existing patterns like how in-flow publishes its snapshots, how live review snapshots work, where panels get mounted in the editor file, and how extensions register, so the new contract follows established conventions. I'm also weighing whether both agents should edit directly in this already-dirty main checkout or whether a separate branch makes more sense given how much uncommitted work is already there.

To avoid conflicts, I'll split ownership cleanly: backend handles the living-desk utils, the editor extension, and only the extension-registration piece of the editor file, while frontend owns the panel components, CSS, and the panel-mounting piece of that same file — both touching the same file but in different regions, which should be safe as long as each agent re-reads before editing.

Actually, it might be simpler if I just own the integration wiring myself at the end — having each agent expose a clean entry point that I connect, rather than both editing the shared file directly. Let me check how similar features like the in-flow or margin-rail components are mounted to decide the right pattern before assigning tasks.
Both gpt-6.1-sol and claude-sonnet-5-5 are available for delegation. I'll first map out the integration points so both agents work against a shared contract without overlapping on the same files.

content.thinking:
I'm planning to assign Codex GPT-6.1 on high reasoning to handle backend implementation while Sonnet on low handles frontend, and I need to divide the work carefully so both agents editing the same checkout don't conflict with each other.

Since a worktree would risk losing the uncommitted changes already in the tree, they both need to work directly in the existing checkout, so I'll define a shared interface contract and clear file ownership first. I'm sketching out the backend engine's architecture — a pure-function module that takes a document snapshot and computes style consistency ledgers like spelling variants, serial comma usage, number formatting, dash and quote styles, and naming consistency across the text.

For stance tracking, I want to count first-person-singular versus plural pronoun usage, flag inclusive-"we" phrases like "as we'll see" or "let's" to avoid false positives, and surface remaining cases as "possible editorial we" with a preview of switching to "I" — leaving deeper classification (the Jev Choice framework) as a refinement rather than claiming certainty from code alone, though since the user's headline example was about royal we, I'm leaning toward wiring in that classification now rather than deferring it.

For the presence grid I'm planning to track capitalized multiword entities appearing at least twice across sections, skipping tense tracking since that needs POS tagging and probably isn't worth the complexity yet. For the live scoring utility, I'm sketching reusing the static feature scorer on a debounce, combined with the last confirmed rubric grade to produce a live estimate, though per-paragraph attribution is something to defer.

For impact calculation, I'm thinking I need to map ledger findings to rubric criteria — stance to voice, naming conventions maybe to integrity or vocabulary — with impact computed as weight times a capped occurrence ratio, labeled clearly as approximate since this is heuristic. I'm checking the rubric criteria list to confirm what weights are assigned to each dimension.

Now I'm sketching the document-ledger extension itself: a ProseMirror controller that debounces document changes, builds a snapshot, runs the ledgers, and broadcasts results through a window event similar to the existing flow event. It also needs to manage decorations per active lens and expose controller methods for setting the lens, applying fixes to specific or all occurrences, and marking findings as deliberate — persisting that state locally for now with Charter integration deferred to later.

I also need the controller to handle jumping to an occurrence and computing its screen coordinates so the spine strip can position ticks correctly, likely via a `coords(pos)` method relative to the editor mount. Then I'm planning the `startLivingDesk` hookup function wired into the main editor component alongside the existing flow conductor, and sketching the frontend pieces — a document spine strip with section bands and lens ticks, plus a card list component for surfaced findings.

Now I'm figuring out where the Living Desk cards panel should actually live within the UI — whether it's a new toggleable right-side panel or nested in the existing writing tools panel — and checking how the editorial context panel system is structured to decide.

Since the user wants solid design guidance, I should also draft a design spec document covering placement and layout decisions for the Living Desk feature.

For file ownership, I'm planning the split between Codex and myself: Codex handles the engine, ledgers, scoring, event contracts, the editor extension, and wiring into the main editor plus tests, including stance classification work.

For Sonnet's side, I need the React components and CSS — likely a new dedicated CSS file following the existing pattern — plus mounting into the manuscript panel and toggle. The tricky part is that twyne-editor.tsx gets touched by both of us, so I need to decide how to split those edits to avoid collisions, possibly having Codex mount my component at a spot I specify.

Sonnet mounts the living desk panel in manuscript-panel.tsx with visibility tied to the engine snapshot's open state, plus a small toggle tab on the page edge. Codex handles the command registry piece — adding a keybinding/command that dispatches the toggle event, since that touches editor-commands.ts.

Now I need to gather the rubric weights, design tokens, panel structure, live-review snapshot API, askJudgement signature, and system-one budget API before writing the contract file and design doc, then delegating.

I'll finalize the shared contract and design spec first, so Codex and Sonnet can work in parallel without conflicts. Starting with a quick check of the rubric weights, design tokens, and live-review API they'll depend on.

content.thinking:
Now I'm setting up the shared contract file for the living desk, defining the dependency-free types that connect the engine and UI layers for whole-piece findings that stay live as the writer edits.

Still defining types...

Still defining data types...

Finishing the controller interface definition...

Now I'm wondering where the snapshot and controller accessor functions should live — following the struggle-tracker pattern, they'd be exported from the extension module, but that creates a question about the UI importing from that module.

I think the cleanest approach is to put the registry — a module-level snapshot holder, controller holder, and a publish function — directly in the contract file so it has no dependencies on the extension, and both sides can safely import from it.

Now I need to figure out how the live review rubric score maps into my criteria structure. Since the rubric produces its own criterion ids that might not match my CriterionKey set, I'll keep things generic by using plain string keys and labels for criteria and matching findings by string, letting Codex handle the mapping flexibly.

The static feature scorer produces scores for length, structure, pacing, evidence, vocabulary, paragraph shape, and integrity — but not voice. That's a problem since a stance-related fix wouldn't move any visible score. The user wants fixes to visibly affect something, so I'm thinking of adding a consistency criterion computed from the ledgers themselves — stance mix, naming variants, style sheet inconsistencies — something code can compute directly rather than relying on the rubric.

# Living desk: design guidance

Companion to `docs/writing-instruments.md`. This governs how the living desk looks, moves, and speaks. The contract is `src/utils/living-desk-contract.ts`.

## What it should feel like

A copyeditor's style sheet and a proofreader's pencil, not a dashboard. The writer should feel the piece being *watched over*, never *graded at*. Three tests decide every detail:

1. **Cause and effect are visible.** Every fix produces three linked reactions at once: the span in the manuscript, the card's count, and the score. If any one of the three is missing, the moment feels fake.
2. **The manuscript stays the hero.** The desk recolours the page; it never covers it. Nothing animates while the writer types.
3. **Nothing is claimed that wasn't measured.** Estimates carry ≈. Model classifications carry their probability. Rule findings say "by rule".

## Spatial logic

- **Left is the piece; right is the passage.** The right margin already holds passage notes (flow rail, in-flow tools). The desk and the spine sit on the left, beside the outline, because they are about the whole document.
- **Panel:** a fixed aside on the left, in the same slot as the outline panel (`top: 5rem; bottom: 4rem; left: 1rem; width: 20rem`). Opening one closes the other. Below 64rem viewport width it becomes a bottom sheet capped at 55vh.
- **Spine:** a 6px strip hugging the page's left edge for the full height of the manuscript. It widens to 12px on hover or focus. Section boundaries are hairlines; occurrences of the active lens are ticks; the focused finding's ticks are full strength and the rest are 35%. The top of the spine carries a small score cap (the estimate, tabular figures) that opens the panel.
- **Hidden when quiet:** no spine in manual Zen, in automatic flow (`html[data-flow]`), or in read-only mode without findings. The desk never reveals itself while the writer types: it can update counts, but it only *opens* on request.

## Visual language

Use the existing tokens only; every theme (foolscap, broadsheet, nightpress) must work without overrides.

| Element | Treatment |
| --- | --- |
| Panel | `--color-paper` background, 1px `--color-paper-3` border, `border-radius: 2px`, the same shadow as `.in-flow-card`. No rounded SaaS corners, no gradients. |
| Section heads in the panel | `.dept-label` (typewriter, uppercase, 0.32em tracking, `--color-ink-muted`). |
| Card | Like `.in-flow-card`: 2px radius, `--color-paper` on a `--color-paper-2` panel, 3px left rule coloured by lens. Kicker = level in `.dept-label` style. Title in `--font-display` 600, 0.9375rem. Metric in `--font-serif` italic 0.8125rem `--color-ink-light`. Impact right-aligned in `--font-sans` 0.75rem tabular, `--color-accent-green`. |
| Score | Estimate in `--font-display` 2rem, tabular. A muted "≈" prefix appears only while `editsSinceConfirmed > 0`. Confirmed letter in typewriter beside it. Criteria are hairline bars (4px, `--color-paper-3` track, `--color-ink-muted` fill) labelled in sans 0.75rem, with "by rule" or "by review" beneath in 0.625rem muted. |
| Occurrence rows | Manuscript serif at 0.875rem. Removed text `--color-accent-red` with line-through at 70% opacity; inserted text `--color-accent-green` on `--color-highlight-mint`. Provenance chips in sans 0.6875rem, 1px `--color-paper-3` border, pill radius allowed only here. |

**Lens colours (flagged / context):**

| Lens | Flagged | Context |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stance | `--color-vermilion` underline 2px + `--color-highlight-rose` wash | `--color-cobalt` text weight 600 for "I" |
| Naming | `--color-mustard` wavy underline | `--color-highlight-sky` wash on canonical spelling |
| Style | `--color-text-periwinkle` dotted underline | none |
| Presence | per-entity wash from the persona palette (cobalt, sage, periwinkle, mustard, blush) at 35% | none |

Colour is never the only signal: flagged spans always carry an underline style, and cards say what the colour means in words.

## Manuscript decorations

The engine adds these classes; the interface styles them globally (decorations live inside ProseMirror's DOM).

- `.ld-occ` on every decorated span, with `data-ld-lens` and `data-ld-label`.
- `.ld-occ--flagged`, `.ld-occ--context`, `.ld-occ--focused` (the focused finding), `.ld-occ--previewing` (original text shown struck through during a preview).
- `.ld-ghost` widget immediately after a previewed span: the replacement in italic `--color-accent-green`, with a 1px dashed left rule. It must not shift line breaks more than the replacement itself would.
- `.ld-flash` for 1.2s after a fix lands: `--color-highlight-mint` fading to transparent.
- The editor root gets `data-ld-lens="<lens>"` while a lens is on and `data-ld-focus` while a finding is focused. **Only `data-ld-focus` dims** the rest of the text (to `--color-ink-light`, not lighter); a lens alone just marks occurrences. The dim lifts the moment the caret enters the manuscript and a key is pressed.

## Motion

- Score number: tween 600ms, ease-out cubic. Criterion bar width: 700ms `cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)`; the fill turns `--color-accent-green` for 2.4s after a rise, `--color-accent-amber` after a fall.
- Delta flag: a small pill beside the criterion (`+0.3 · ¶6`) that fades in over 200ms, holds 2.4s, then fades out.
- **No reordering under the pointer.** When a finding resolves or its impact changes, keep the list order until the pointer leaves the list (or 1.5s with no pointer), then reflow with a 200ms FLIP. A card the writer is working in never moves.
- Resolved cards drop to 60% opacity with a ✓ and move to the end on the next reflow.
- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`: no tweens, flashes or FLIP; values change instantly and the delta pill stays static for the same duration.

## Copy

- Name observable things: "3 editorial “we” · 41 “I”", "“Hollis” once in ¶6, “Hollins” 14 times". Never "you seem unsure", never "AI suggests".
- Buttons name the action: "Make it I", "Make all 3 I", "Use “Hollins”", "The mix is deliberate", "Hollis is a different place". Not "Apply", "Accept", "OK".
- Impact: "≈ +0.27". Below 0.05 show "small". Null impact shows the criterion name instead.
- Provenance: "rule", "Jev .88", "model". When judgement is unreachable, a single "rule-only" chip at the top of the panel, with the tooltip "No judgement model reachable, so classifications are by rule."
- Empty: "Nothing across the piece needs you right now." followed by one muted line listing what is watched: "Watching stance, names and the style sheet."
- Short drafts (under about 150 words): "The desk starts reading at about 150 words."
- Deliberate: "Kept on purpose. Twyne will flag only new drift."

## States each card must handle

open · improving (some fixed) · resolved · deliberate · stale (the span moved; show "This changed since it was found" and disable its fix) · read-only (no fix buttons; jump only) · judgement pending (a quiet "reading…" in the metric line, never a spinner).

## Accessibility

- Panel: `<aside aria-label="The piece">`. Each card header is a `<button aria-expanded>`. Fix buttons are real buttons with text labels.
- One polite live region announces score changes: "Consistency up 0.3 after the fix in paragraph 6."
- Keyboard: Escape clears focus and the lens, then closes the panel. Enter on an occurrence row jumps to it. Focus returns to the card after a fix, never to the manuscript.
- Spine ticks are decorative (`aria-hidden`); the same jumps are reachable from the cards.

## Anti-patterns

- Rounded, glossy cards, coloured gradients, emoji, or icons where a word fits.
- Toasts for routine fixes. The reaction belongs where the change happened.
- A score that moves while the writer types prose. Rule criteria may recompute on every edit, but the estimate's *animation* runs only after a fix or a 2s pause.
- A grade shown without saying whether it is confirmed or estimated.
- Opening the panel automatically.

## Acceptance checks

1. Open the desk on a draft with a mixed I/we stance. Fix one occurrence. Within 300ms: the span flashes, the count drops by one, the consistency bar rises with a delta pill naming the paragraph, and the estimate tweens with ≈.
2. Press Undo. Everything returns, including the count and the estimate.
3. Mark the stance finding deliberate, reload: it stays deliberate.
4. Switch theme to nightpress: every lens colour is legible (WCAG AA against the page for text, 3:1 for underlines).
5. Type a paragraph with the panel open: nothing animates, nothing reorders, typing latency is unchanged.

# Living desk: design guidance

Companion to `docs/writing-instruments.md`. This governs how the living desk looks, moves, and speaks. The contract is `src/utils/living-desk-contract.ts`.

## What it should feel like

A copyeditor's style sheet and a proofreader's pencil, not a dashboard. The writer should feel the piece being *watched over*, never *graded at*. Three tests decide every detail:

1. **Cause and effect are visible.** Every fix produces three linked reactions at once: the span in the manuscript, the card's count, and the score. If any one of the three is missing, the moment feels fake.
2. **The manuscript stays the hero.** The desk recolours the page; it never covers it. Nothing animates while the writer types.
3. **Nothing is claimed that wasn't measured.** Estimates carry ≈. Model classifications carry their probability. Rule findings say "by rule".

## Spatial logic

- **Left is the piece; right is the passage.** The right margin already holds passage notes (flow rail, in-flow tools). The desk and the spine sit on the left, beside the outline, because they are about the whole document.
- **Panel:** a fixed aside on the left, in the same slot as the outline panel (`top: 5rem; bottom: 4rem; left: 1rem; width: 20rem`). Opening one closes the other. Below 64rem viewport width it becomes a bottom sheet capped at 55vh.
- **Spine:** a 6px strip hugging the page's left edge for the full height of the manuscript. It widens to 12px on hover or focus. Section boundaries are hairlines; occurrences of the active lens are ticks; the focused finding's ticks are full strength and the rest are 35%. The top of the spine carries a small score cap (the estimate, tabular figures) that opens the panel.
- **Hidden when quiet:** no spine in manual Zen, in automatic flow (`html[data-flow]`), or in read-only mode without findings. The desk never reveals itself while the writer types: it can update counts, but it only *opens* on request.

## Visual language

Use the existing tokens only; every theme (foolscap, broadsheet, nightpress) must work without overrides.

| Element | Treatment |
| --- | --- |
| Panel | `--color-paper` background, 1px `--color-paper-3` border, `border-radius: 2px`, the same shadow as `.in-flow-card`. No rounded SaaS corners, no gradients. |
| Section heads in the panel | `.dept-label` (typewriter, uppercase, 0.32em tracking, `--color-ink-muted`). |
| Card | Like `.in-flow-card`: 2px radius, `--color-paper` on a `--color-paper-2` panel, 3px left rule coloured by lens. Kicker = level in `.dept-label` style. Title in `--font-display` 600, 0.9375rem. Metric in `--font-serif` italic 0.8125rem `--color-ink-light`. Impact right-aligned in `--font-sans` 0.75rem tabular, `--color-accent-green`. |
| Score | Estimate in `--font-display` 2rem, tabular. A muted "≈" prefix appears only while `editsSinceConfirmed > 0`. Confirmed letter in typewriter beside it. Criteria are hairline bars (4px, `--color-paper-3` track, `--color-ink-muted` fill) labelled in sans 0.75rem, with "by rule" or "by review" beneath in 0.625rem muted. |
| Occurrence rows | Manuscript serif at 0.875rem. Removed text `--color-accent-red` with line-through at 70% opacity; inserted text `--color-accent-green` on `--color-highlight-mint`. Provenance chips in sans 0.6875rem, 1px `--color-paper-3` border, pill radius allowed only here. |

**Lens colours (flagged / context):**

| Lens | Flagged | Context |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stance | `--color-vermilion` underline 2px + `--color-highlight-rose` wash | `--color-cobalt` text weight 600 for "I" |
| Naming | `--color-mustard` wavy underline | `--color-highlight-sky` wash on canonical spelling |
| Style | `--color-text-periwinkle` dotted underline | none |
| Presence | per-entity wash from the persona palette (cobalt, sage, periwinkle, mustard, blush) at 35% | none |

Colour is never the only signal: flagged spans always carry an underline style, and cards say what the colour means in words.

## Manuscript decorations

The engine adds these classes; the interface styles them globally (decorations live inside ProseMirror's DOM).

- `.ld-occ` on every decorated span, with `data-ld-lens` and `data-ld-label`.
- `.ld-occ--flagged`, `.ld-occ--context`, `.ld-occ--focused` (the focused finding), `.ld-occ--previewing` (original text shown struck through during a preview).
- `.ld-ghost` widget immediately after a previewed span: the replacement in italic `--color-accent-green`, with a 1px dashed left rule. It must not shift line breaks more than the replacement itself would.
- `.ld-flash` for 1.2s after a fix lands: `--color-highlight-mint` fading to transparent.
- The editor root gets `data-ld-lens="<lens>"` while a lens is on and `data-ld-focus` while a finding is focused. **Only `data-ld-focus` dims** the rest of the text (to `--color-ink-light`, not lighter); a lens alone just marks occurrences. The dim lifts the moment the caret enters the manuscript and a key is pressed.

## Motion

- Score number: tween 600ms, ease-out cubic. Criterion bar width: 700ms `cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)`; the fill turns `--color-accent-green` for 2.4s after a rise, `--color-accent-amber` after a fall.
- Delta flag: a small pill beside the criterion (`+0.3 · ¶6`) that fades in over 200ms, holds 2.4s, then fades out.
- **No reordering under the pointer.** When a finding resolves or its impact changes, keep the list order until the pointer leaves the list (or 1.5s with no pointer), then reflow with a 200ms FLIP. A card the writer is working in never moves.
- Resolved cards drop to 60% opacity with a ✓ and move to the end on the next reflow.
- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`: no tweens, flashes or FLIP; values change instantly and the delta pill stays static for the same duration.

## Copy

- Name observable things: "3 editorial “we” · 41 “I”", "“Hollis” once in ¶6, “Hollins” 14 times". Never "you seem unsure", never "AI suggests".
- Buttons name the action: "Make it I", "Make all 3 I", "Use “Hollins”", "The mix is deliberate", "Hollis is a different place". Not "Apply", "Accept", "OK".
- Impact: "≈ +0.27". Below 0.05 show "small". Null impact shows the criterion name instead.
- Provenance: "rule", "Jev .88", "model". When judgement is unreachable, a single "rule-only" chip at the top of the panel, with the tooltip "No judgement model reachable, so classifications are by rule."
- Empty: "Nothing across the piece needs you right now." followed by one muted line listing what is watched: "Watching stance, names and the style sheet."
- Short drafts (under about 150 words): "The desk starts reading at about 150 words."
- Deliberate: "Kept on purpose. Twyne will flag only new drift."

## States each card must handle

open · improving (some fixed) · resolved · deliberate · stale (the span moved; show "This changed since it was found" and disable its fix) · read-only (no fix buttons; jump only) · judgement pending (a quiet "reading…" in the metric line, never a spinner).

## Accessibility

- Panel: `<aside aria-label="The piece">`. Each card header is a `<button aria-expanded>`. Fix buttons are real buttons with text labels.
- One polite live region announces score changes: "Consistency up 0.3 after the fix in paragraph 6."
- Keyboard: Escape clears focus and the lens, then closes the panel. Enter on an occurrence row jumps to it. Focus returns to the card after a fix, never to the manuscript.
- Spine ticks are decorative (`aria-hidden`); the same jumps are reachable from the cards.

## Anti-patterns

- Rounded, glossy cards, coloured gradients, emoji, or icons where a word fits.
- Toasts for routine fixes. The reaction belongs where the change happened.
- A score that moves while the writer types prose. Rule criteria may recompute on every edit, but the estimate's *animation* runs only after a fix or a 2s pause.
- A grade shown without saying whether it is confirmed or estimated.
- Opening the panel automatically.

## Acceptance checks

1. Open the desk on a draft with a mixed I/we stance. Fix one occurrence. Within 300ms: the span flashes, the count drops by one, the consistency bar rises with a delta pill naming the paragraph, and the estimate tweens with ≈.
2. Press Undo. Everything returns, including the count and the estimate.
3. Mark the stance finding deliberate, reload: it stays deliberate.
4. Switch theme to nightpress: every lens colour is legible (WCAG AA against the page for text, 3:1 for underlines).
5. Type a paragraph with the panel open: nothing animates, nothing reorders, typing latency is unchanged.

I'm splitting the work into two delegated tasks: a backend engine covering analysis modules, editor extension wiring, controller, scoring, persistence, and stance classification with tests, and a lighter frontend task for the panel UI, spine, cards, decoration styling, and toggle controls mounted into the manuscript panel.

Since both run concurrently in the same checkout, I need to carve out clear file ownership to avoid conflicts — backend owns the living-desk utils and extension files plus the single wiring edit in twyne-editor.tsx that starts the feature, while frontend mounts its panel from manuscript-panel.tsx instead of touching twyne-editor.tsx directly. I'm figuring out how the toggle and "close the other panel" behavior should work through an event dispatch rather than frontend editing the outline store directly.

I'm also deciding the toggle button should live in the Review tab of the compositor toolbar, owned by frontend, dispatching a toggle event that the engine listens for and persists via a stored open-state key — so frontend just fires the event and the engine handles state. Still weighing whether i18n string handling for the UI needs to be flagged for frontend's component patterns.

For the pure engine modules, I'm sketching segment.ts to turn a ProseMirror document into labeled text blocks (paragraphs, headings, section splits, numbering, offset-to-position mapping), with logic to skip quoted dialogue, blockquotes, and code blocks. Then stance.ts needs to detect first-person singular and plural pronouns outside those excluded zones, following similar skip rules.

For stance classification, I'm working through heuristics without an LLM: distinguishing inclusive "we" (as in "let's consider") from ambiguous group references, defaulting unclassified plurals to a neutral label, and firing a finding when singular first-person dominates (count ≥3, share ≥0.6) alongside plural occurrences, while separately flagging editorial "we" patterns like "we argue" or "in our view" under a distinct rule-based label.

With an LLM available instead, I'd classify each plural occurrence into one of five categories (author alone, author+reader, group author belongs to, quoted speaker, people in general), feeding sentence context and batching requests efficiently with caching, flagging cases where author-alone probability is high. Then for the actual text fix, I'm mapping we→I, us→me, our→my, ourselves→myself, plus adjusting verb agreement for contractions like "we're"→"I'm" and "we've"→"I've".

I also need to handle case preservation for capitalized "We"→"I" and decide whether to run this stance detection only on English text, likely gating it on an existing language detection check rather than building something new.

For the naming module, I'm planning to detect capitalized tokens outside sentence starts, group similar-looking variants using edit distance thresholds scaled to word length, then flag the less common variant when a canonical form dominates, while excluding common words via a small stoplist to avoid false positives. For the style-sheet module, I want to check consistency in serial comma usage and numeral formatting across the document.

I'm also sketching rules for number spelling, US/UK spelling pairs, dash spacing, quote style, and informal word variants, applying a majority-rule approach so minority usages get flagged and converted. Then for presence detection, I'm reusing the canonical entity names from naming to count mentions per section and surface findings when an entity recurs across multiple sections.

For the gap-detection piece, I'm flagging entities that appear across sections but have a visible absence span in between, as long as the document has enough sections to make that meaningful — like noting a character disappearing from one section before resurfacing later. I'm also wiring up the live scoring system to pull from debounced static feature checks (evidence, pacing, vocabulary, integrity, paragraph shape, structure) and computing a consistency score that deducts points for flagged stance issues, naming variants, and style minority cases, capped at a floor of zero.

Now I'm working out how review scores should update live — estimating confirmed scores plus deltas from rule-based criteria since the last confirmation, or falling back to a weighted mean when nothing's confirmed yet, and tying impact calculations to how much resolving a finding would improve the consistency score, with effort scaled to flagged count.

For the live-review trigger, I'm considering having Codex add an exported `requestLiveReview()` or a dedicated event that live-review.ts listens for, bypassing the normal 30-second throttle, since live review already requires 500+ words and a connected client. I'm also checking how the confirmed grade maps from RubricResult.overallScore into a 0-10 scale.

Now I'm planning the LivingDeskDecorations Tiptap extension — a plugin that maintains a decoration set updated via transaction meta, which needs to be registered alongside the editor's other extensions like InFlowAnchor in twyne-editor.tsx. I also need a `startLivingDesk` function that debounces recomputation on document changes, caps processing at a character limit for performance, and triggers classification after the document settles.

Still planning the controller: askJudgement should work without requiring a client (fixing an audit gap), budgeted through system-one-budget. The applyFix logic verifies text at the given range still matches before applying a fix (falling back to nearby search in the paragraph), runs as a single undoable transaction, flashes a decoration, and recomputes immediately for fast feedback — while applyAll processes occurrences from the end backward, previews use ghost decorations, and deliberate markings persist per-folio via localStorage/IndexedDB, deferring Charter rule integration for later.

I'm setting lens/focus attributes on the editor DOM, clearing focus on keydown, computing scroll position via coordsAtPos relative to the view's bounding rect, and handling jump-to-position/section with selection, scroll, and focus. I'm also adding open/close toggle persistence, skipping heavy publishing when a flow attribute is present, wiring the living-desk startup and decorations extension into twyne-editor.tsx inside the active-folio/non-readonly block, and planning bun tests for the pure stance and naming modules.

I'm now mapping out additional unit tests for style sheet rules, presence gaps, and score estimation math, plus extension controller fix application using the existing headless Tiptap test harness, along with verification commands for running tests, type-checking, and linting. Then I'm sketching the frontend living-desk panel component—subscribing to the living-desk event, rendering the score block, lens filter chips, and an expandable card list with diff-style occurrence rows.

Writing document spine component...

I'm also working through the CSS import strategy, realizing decoration classes need global (not scoped) styles since they target raw ProseMirror DOM, so useStyles$ is the right choice over useStylesScoped$.

For mounting, I'll place the DocumentSpine and LivingDeskPanel after FlowSurface in manuscript-panel.tsx, hiding them via CSS when zen mode or flow state is active. I still need to find where the toggle button should live, likely in the compositor's Review tab toolbar.

I also want a Storybook story for the panel using a fixture snapshot, since the backend engine is being built concurrently — the panel should accept an optional snapshot prop so I can develop against mock data independently.

I should avoid touching the contract file and living-desk core modules directly (flag needed changes instead), and keep the worktree clean — no commits, deploys, stashes, or resets, and don't disturb unrelated in-progress changes from others.

Both tasks run async, so I'll integrate and review once they're done. I need to include design doc paths, the contract reference, and the CLAUDE.md Convex guideline reminder (backend work shouldn't touch convex/ directly). For i18n, selection-actions just uses plain strings, so that's fine as-is. Now I'll draft the actual delegate task calls.
With the contract and design spec ready, I'm assigning the engine to Codex and the interface to Sonnet 5.5, each with clear file ownership so they can work in parallel without conflicts.

You are implementing the ENGINE for Twyne's "living desk", Phase 1. Repo: /home/diogenes/Projects/apps/twyne (Qwik + Tiptap/ProseMirror + Convex, bun). A separate agent is building the INTERFACE in parallel in the same checkout, so respect the file ownership below exactly.

## Read first
1. `src/utils/living-desk-contract.ts`: the ONLY contract between you and the interface. Implement it faithfully. Do NOT change its exported types or names. If you truly need a change, keep it additive (optional fields only) and list it in your final report.
2. `docs/living-desk-design.md`: the design spec. The "Manuscript decorations" section defines the classes and attributes you must emit. The "Copy" section defines the wording for titles, metrics and notes, which you produce.
3. `docs/writing-instruments.md`: sections "Levels", "Consistency ledgers", "The living score".
4. Patterns to copy: `src/components/editor/extensions/struggle-tracker.ts` (module-level snapshot + controller + publish via window CustomEvent, ProseMirror decoration plugin `InFlowAnchor`, the `ask` helper with `systemOneWait/spendSystemOne/backOffSystemOne` from `src/utils/system-one-budget.ts`), `src/utils/system-one.ts` (choice/noul builders, isChoice), `src/utils/judgement-client.ts` (`askJudgement`), `src/utils/rubric.ts` (`scoreStaticFeatures`), `src/utils/live-review.ts` (`liveReviewSnapshot`, event `twyne:live-review`), `src/utils/passage-triage.ts` (batching Jev questions).
5. Repo rules: CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md. Do not touch `convex/`.

## Files you own (create/edit only these)
- NEW `src/utils/living-desk/` (pure, DOM-free, unit-tested analysis modules)
- NEW `src/components/editor/extensions/living-desk.ts` (Tiptap extension + `startLivingDesk`)
- `src/components/editor/twyne-editor.tsx`: ONLY (a) register your decoration extension where the other editor extensions (e.g. `InFlowAnchor`) are registered and (b) add `cleanup(startLivingDesk(editor, {...}))` inside the existing `if (activeFolioId && !readOnly) {` block next to `startFlowConductor`. Nothing else in that file.
- `src/utils/live-review.ts`: ONLY to add a listener for a new window event `twyne:live-review-request` that schedules a review promptly (bypassing the 30 s spacing, still respecting its other gates). Add that event name as an exported const in `living-desk-contract.ts` (additive) or in live-review.ts.
- Tests next to your modules (`*.test.ts`).
The interface agent owns `src/components/living-desk/**`, `src/components/editor/manuscript-panel.tsx`, compositor/toolbar files and all CSS. Do not edit those. Do not write CSS; just emit the documented classes.

## What to build

### Pure analysis (src/utils/living-desk/)
Input: a lightweight segment model of the doc. Build it in a `segment.ts` that walks a ProseMirror `Node` into blocks `{kind: paragraph|heading|quote|code|other, text, pos (doc position of the block's content start), paragraph number, section index}` plus `sections: SectionInfo[]` split at headings (text before the first heading = "Opening"). Provide an offset→doc-position mapper that handles inline non-text nodes (see `posAtOffset` in struggle-tracker.ts). Keep the analysis functions taking plain data so they are testable without an editor. Skip quote/code blocks and text inside quotation marks ("…", “…”) for stance.

1. `stance.ts`: the I/we ledger.
   - Find first-person singular (I, me, my, mine, myself) and plural (we, us, our, ours, ourselves, let's) outside quotes/blockquotes/code.
   - The finding exists only when the piece is mainly singular: at least 3 singular and singular ≥ 60% of first-person tokens, and at least one plural.
   - Rule labels: inclusive ("as we'll see", "as we have seen", "let us/let's" + verb, "we can see"); group ("we" + a plural noun such as kids, children, students, villagers, "we both", "we all", "my family and I… we"); editorial ("we would argue", "we argue", "we contend", "we believe", "we must admit", "we think", "in our view", "our view", "our argument", "our thesis", "we have shown", "we will show"). Everything else is `unclassified` (shown, not flagged).
   - With Jev (when available): batch one Choice per unclassified-or-rule-labelled plural occurrence with options exactly ["the author alone (an editorial or royal we)", "the author and the reader together", "a group the author belongs to", "a character or quoted speaker", "people in general"]. State: the sentence, the previous sentence, and the counts of singular vs plural. At most 24 questions per request, cached by sentence text. Flag only when P(author alone) ≥ 0.6. Record the probability and a short note ("the author alone"). Jev overrides rule labels.
   - Deterministic fix per flagged occurrence, case preserved: we→I, us→me, our→my, ours→mine, ourselves→myself. Agreement with the immediately following verb: are→am, were→was, 're→'m, 've/'d/'ll stay, "we were"→"I was", "we are"→"I am". The occurrence span covers the pronoun plus the agreeing verb when that changes. Test all of this.
   - Finding id `stance`, lens `stance`, level `piece`, criterion `consistency`, title "Editorial “we” in an “I” essay", metric like `3 editorial “we” · 41 “I”`. Include context occurrences (flagged:false) for inclusive and group cases with a note.
2. `naming.ts`: capitalised name tokens and multi-word names not at sentence start. Group spelling variants: Damerau-Levenshtein ≤1 for length ≥5, ≤2 for length ≥8, same first letter, and the canonical form appears ≥2× as often. Exclude a stoplist of common capitalised words. One finding per group, id `naming:<canonical lowercased>`, lens `naming`, level `piece`, criterion `consistency`, fix = the canonical spelling. Title like `Hollins is spelled two ways`; metric `“Hollins” ×14 · “Hollis” ×1 in ¶6`.
3. `style-sheet.ts`: majority-rule consistency. One finding per rule that has a minority, fix = convert to the majority form:
   - serial comma
   - US/UK spelling pairs (a table of ~40 pairs, e.g. color/colour, center/centre, -ize/-ise, gray/grey, toward/towards)
   - spelled-out vs digit numbers below 10 (exclude dates, times, measurements, decimals)
   - spaced vs closed em dash
   - curly vs straight quotes
   Lens `style`, level `piece`, criterion `consistency`, provenance `rule`, ids `style:<rule>`.
4. `presence.ts`: entities = canonical names with ≥2 mentions. Build counts per section into `PresenceRow[]`. A finding when the doc has ≥3 sections and an entity present in ≥2 sections is absent from ≥1 section between appearances: id `presence:<name>`, lens `presence`, level `section`, criterion `structure`, impact null, actions ["jump"], occurrences = the last mention before the gap and the first after (flagged:false). Title e.g. `Mara Okafor drops out of §II` (use the section titles if short, otherwise §n).
5. `score.ts`: the live score.
   - Rule criteria from `scoreStaticFeatures(plainText)`: evidence, pacing, vocabulary, integrity, paragraphShape, structure. Use the labels from rubric.ts where they exist. scope `paragraph`, source `rule`.
   - Plus a `consistency` criterion = 10 − penalties: 0.3 per flagged stance occurrence, 0.4 per naming variant occurrence, 0.1 per style minority occurrence, capped total penalty 6.
   - Review criteria from `liveReviewSnapshot().review?.rubric?.judgementGrade` (scope piece, source review), updated on the `twyne:live-review` event.
   - Confirmed grade = the review's grade on a 0–10 scale (read rubric-grade.ts / types to convert correctly) plus the letter.
   - Estimate = confirmed + Σ w_k·(rule_k_now − rule_k_at_confirm) using normalised rule weights (reuse FEATURE_WEIGHTS where possible; give consistency a weight comparable to vocabulary). Without a confirmed read, estimate = the weighted mean of rule criteria. Clamp 0–10. Do not show an estimate under ~150 words: null.
   - `impact` per finding = weight(criterion) × (consistency if that finding were resolved − consistency now), computed by recomputing the penalty without it. `effort` = flagged count.
   - Sort findings: open by impact desc, null-impact after open, then improving, resolved, deliberate.
   - `delta` per criterion = value − value at confirm.
   - `lastChange` set after a fix: criterion with the largest change, its delta, and source `¶<n>`.

### Editor extension (src/components/editor/extensions/living-desk.ts)
- `LivingDeskDecorations` Tiptap Extension: a plugin holding a DecorationSet set via meta and mapped through transactions. Emit inline decorations with classes `ld-occ`, `ld-occ--flagged|--context`, `ld-occ--focused`, `ld-occ--previewing` and attributes `data-ld-lens`, `data-ld-label`, `data-ld-id`. Emit a widget `.ld-ghost` after a previewed span containing the replacement text, and `.ld-flash` inline decorations for ~1.2 s after a fix. Only decorate occurrences of the active lens (or the focused finding's lens). Set `data-ld-lens` / `data-ld-focus` attributes on `editor.view.dom` while a lens or focus is active. Remove `data-ld-focus` on the first keydown in the editor.
- `startLivingDesk(editor, { getClient, folioId })` returns cleanup:
  - Recompute rule analyses on doc change, debounced 400 ms, and immediately after a fix.
  - Skip transactions from y-sync / `addToHistory:false` for counting edits, like flow-conductor does.
  - Cap analysis cost (measure; it must not add typing latency: run off the keystroke path, consider requestIdleCallback, bail above ~80k chars to sections near the cursor if needed).
  - Run the Jev stance classification ≥2 s after the last edit for new unclassified sentences, via `askJudgement(getClient(), …)`. Do NOT require a Convex client before calling: askJudgement handles the endpoint transport itself. Respect the shared budget, and set `judgement` to `offline` when unavailable and `reading` while in flight.
  - Persist deliberate finding ids per folio (localStorage key `living-desk-deliberate:<folioId>`).
  - Persist open state under `LIVING_DESK_OPEN_KEY`. Listen for `LIVING_DESK_TOGGLE_EVENT` (detail.open optional).
  - Register the controller via `registerLivingDeskController` and publish via `publishLivingDesk`.
- Controller semantics:
  - applyFix verifies the doc text at [from,to] equals `occurrence.text`. If not, re-find it within the same paragraph; otherwise return false and mark that finding stale-safe. Apply as ONE undoable transaction, flash it, and republish within the same frame so the interface sees count + score change < 300 ms.
  - applyAll applies every flagged fix of a finding in ONE transaction, from the end backwards.
  - Undo must naturally restore counts (recompute on doc change).
  - jumpTo selects and scrolls into view.
  - spineFraction(pos) = (coordsAtPos(pos).top − dom top) / dom scrollHeight, null on failure.

Agreement with the immediately following verb: are→am, were→was, 're→'m, 've/'d/'ll stay, "we were"→"I was", "we are"→"I am". The occurrence span covers the pronoun plus the agreeing verb when that changes. Test all of this.
   - Finding id `stance`, lens `stance`, level `piece`, criterion `consistency`, title "Editorial “we” in an “I” essay", metric like `3 editorial “we” · 41 “I”`. Include context occurrences (flagged:false) for inclusive and group cases with a note.
2. `naming.ts`: capitalised name tokens and multi-word names not at sentence start. Group spelling variants: Damerau-Levenshtein ≤1 for length ≥5, ≤2 for length ≥8, same first letter, and the canonical form appears ≥2× as often. Exclude a stoplist of common capitalised words. One finding per group, id `naming:<canonical lowercased>`, lens `naming`, level `piece`, criterion `consistency`, fix = the canonical spelling. Title like `Hollins is spelled two ways`; metric `“Hollins” ×14 · “Hollis” ×1 in ¶6`.
3. `style-sheet.ts`: majority-rule consistency. One finding per rule that has a minority, fix = convert to the majority form:
   - serial comma
   - US/UK spelling pairs (a table of ~40 pairs, e.g. color/colour, center/centre, -ize/-ise, gray/grey, toward/towards)
   - spelled-out vs digit numbers below 10 (exclude dates, times, measurements, decimals)
   - spaced vs closed em dash
   - curly vs straight quotes
   Lens `style`, level `piece`, criterion `consistency`, provenance `rule`, ids `style:<rule>`.
4. `presence.ts`: entities = canonical names with ≥2 mentions. Build counts per section into `PresenceRow[]`. A finding when the doc has ≥3 sections and an entity present in ≥2 sections is absent from ≥1 section between appearances: id `presence:<name>`, lens `presence`, level `section`, criterion `structure`, impact null, actions ["jump"], occurrences = the last mention before the gap and the first after (flagged:false). 5. `score.ts`: the live score.
   - Rule criteria from `scoreStaticFeatures(plainText)`: evidence, pacing, vocabulary, integrity, paragraphShape, structure. Use the labels from rubric.ts where they exist. scope `paragraph`, source `rule`.
   - Plus a `consistency` criterion = 10 − penalties: 0.3 per flagged stance occurrence, 0.4 per naming variant occurrence, 0.1 per style minority occurrence, capped total penalty 6.
   - Review criteria from `liveReviewSnapshot().review?.rubric?.judgementGrade` (scope piece, source review), updated on the `twyne:live-review` event.
   - Confirmed grade = the review's grade on a 0–10 scale (read rubric-grade.ts / types to convert correctly) plus the letter.
   - Estimate = confirmed + Σ w_k·(rule_k_now − rule_k_at_confirm) using normalised rule weights (reuse FEATURE_WEIGHTS where possible; give consistency a weight comparable to vocabulary). Without a confirmed read, estimate = the weighted mean of rule criteria. Clamp 0–10. Do not show an estimate under ~150 words: null.
   - `impact` per finding = weight(criterion) × (consistency if that finding were resolved − consistency now), computed by recomputing the penalty without it. `effort` = flagged count.
   - Sort findings: open by impact desc, null-impact after open, then improving, resolved, deliberate.
   - `delta` per criterion = value − value at confirm.
   - `lastChange` set after a fix: criterion with the largest change, its delta, and source `¶<n>`.

  - Keep that change minimal and in the existing button style. If adding a keyboard shortcut is trivial via `src/utils/keybindings.ts`, add Mod-Alt-P. Otherwise skip it and say so.
Do NOT edit: `src/utils/living-desk-contract.ts`, `src/utils/living-desk/**`, `src/components/editor/extensions/**`, `src/components/editor/twyne-editor.tsx`, `src/utils/live-review.ts`, anything under `convex/`.

## Behaviour notes
- Subscribe with `useVisibleTask$`. Read `livingDeskSnapshot()` once on mount, then listen for `LIVING_DESK_EVENT`. Call `livingDeskController()` lazily at click time; it can be null when no editor is mounted, in which case disable the actions.
- Never steal the editor selection on mousedown inside the panel (`preventdefault:mousedown` on buttons that act on the doc).
- Nothing animates while the writer types:
  - Tween the estimate (600 ms ease-out cubic) only when `score.lastChange.at` is newer than the last tween, or after a 2 s gap since the previous snapshot.
  - Bars animate width over 700 ms `cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)`. The fill turns green for 2.4 s after a rise and amber after a fall.

- The panel never opens on its own.

- `bunx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` (or `bun run build.types`) and `bunx eslint` on your files must be clean for what you added.
- Build Storybook stories for visual checking. If you can run Storybook or a quick browser render, screenshot the default and nightpress stories and check them against the spec's acceptance checks 1, 4 and 5. Fix contrast or layout problems you see.
- The worktree has many unrelated uncommitted changes from the user. Never revert, stash, reset, or reformat files you don't own. Do not commit.

## Final report
List the files created/changed, screenshots (absolute paths) if you made them, which spec items are done or deferred, any contract changes you need, and anything you assumed about the engine's output.

content.text:
Both agents are now building Phase 1 in parallel:

- **Engine:** Codex on GPT-6.1-Sol, high reasoning, Fast tier.
- **Interface:** Sonnet 5.5 on low.

Before handing off, I wrote three things myself.

**The shared contract** (`src/utils/living-desk-contract.ts`). It's the only thing the two halves share, so neither has to wait for the other. It defines:
- what a finding and an occurrence look like;
- the live score;
- the controller the interface calls (`applyFix`, `applyAll`, `preview`, `markDeliberate`, `jumpTo`, `confirm`);
- the events the engine sends out.

**The design guidance** (`docs/living-desk-design.md`). It's built around three tests:
1. Every fix visibly changes three things together: the text, the card's count, and the score.
2. The manuscript stays central; nothing animates while you type.
3. Nothing claims more than was measured: estimates show ≈, model labels show their probability.

The rest is concrete:
- the piece-level desk and the spine sit on the left; the right margin stays for notes on single passages;
- only your existing paper and ink colour tokens and typefaces, with an assigned colour per lens;
- timings for animations and a rule that cards never reorder under your pointer;
- button labels name the action ("Make it I", "Hollis is a different place");
- accessibility requirements, things to avoid, and five acceptance checks.

**File ownership.** Each agent has a list of files it may edit. Codex makes only two small edits to the editor itself: one start call and one extension registration. Neither agent will commit or touch anything else in your uncommitted work.

What Phase 1 covers:
- **Engine (Codex):**
  - *I/we stance:* code finds the obvious cases, Jev classifies the ambiguous ones, and the fix adjusts the verb ("we were" → "I was").
  - *Name spellings:* catches variants like "Hollins" vs "Hollis".
  - *Style sheet:* serial comma, US vs UK spelling, numbers as digits or words, dash spacing, curly vs straight quotes.
  - *Presence:* tracks where each name appears across sections.
  - *Live score:* rule-based criteria that update on every edit, a "consistency" criterion, and an estimate built on the last confirmed review.
  - *Stance without a Convex sign-in:* the stance check calls Jev even without a Convex client. This removes a gate the audit flagged, but only for this feature.
- **Interface (Sonnet):**
  - the "The piece" panel and the document spine;
  - lens highlighting in the manuscript, with ghost-text previews;
  - Storybook stories built on the flood-memoir example;
  - a toggle on the Review toolbar.

When both finish, I'll review the code against the contract and the design spec, check that the two halves connect, run the tests and type checks, and test it in the running editor. Then I'll report back.
